steps.content: [Background - Dining Car]
The whistle blows once more.
The steam train hurtles through the night, heading toward its final destination. No matter what transpires within its carriages, it will not slow or stop, not even for a moment.
The first-class passengers gather in the dining car. The whispers have ceased. Each person sits there, burdened with their own thoughts. They are all waiting for one final person to arrive.
[Transition for 1s, sliding door sound, Chief's portrait appears]

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: My apologies for keeping you waiting.
No one speaks. Silence hangs heavy in the air, like a blade that's poised to fall. Every pair of eyes is locked onto you, waiting for the gavel to strike.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Time is short, so I'll cut to the chase. Let's settle this quickly.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Today—or rather, last night—a brutal murder took place aboard the Praeva. Who killed her? And why? We must uncover the truth before this train reaches its destination.
Your gaze sweeps across the room before settling on an elderly woman with white hair.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The crime scene was locked from the inside. For this reason, <color=#fb9259>Mrs. Jones</color>, your room is the only path that could lead to it at the time.
Every passenger's gaze turns toward the elderly Mary Jones. The man leaning against the bar seems lost in thought for a moment, then speaks up—

steps.speaker: Carl
steps.content: But the fatal wound on the victim's chest is extremely deep. An elderly woman hardly has the strength for that.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're right. Mrs. Jones wouldn't have the strength to inflict such a deep wound. Which means someone else must have slipped into her room—

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Like a certain <color=#fb9259>train attendant</color> who carelessly left behind a button, for example.
The train attendant Allison shrinks back a step, but before you can press further, William interjects:

steps.speaker: William
steps.content: But there's another uniform in your room.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yes. I initially suspected Ms. Allison. That is until I discovered another train attendant uniform on this train, as well as a spare master key.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then, who else was present that night? Who else could have entered Room 103 when the crime occurred?

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Mr. William, could it have been you?

steps.speaker: Attendant Allison
steps.content: I saw Mr. William in the corridor! He had just finished fixing the circuit breaker, it couldn't possibly have been him!

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...That's also right. And it's not just Mr. William. Everyone in the first-class compartments has an alibi.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Which means there's only one possibility left...

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Last night, an intruder boarded the first-class carriage and murdered the victim amidst the darkness.</color>
You pause. Everyone holds their breath, waiting for you to continue. The old woman hesitantly asks—

steps.speaker: Mrs. Jones
steps.content: You mean... the killer is no longer on the train?

Allison finally lets out a sigh of relief, and the tension in the compartment eases. You look around at each face. Some show relief, while others are tinged with melancholy. Then, you slowly continue.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No. The killer must still be aboard the Praeva.

steps.speaker: The crowd
steps.content: What?

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The Praeva is traveling at speeds of up to 100 kilometers per hour. If the killer had truly jumped off, they would be dead by now. No sane person would choose to do such a thing.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Moreover... there's a far more reasonable explanation for all of this, isn't there? For instance...

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>What if there was more than one killer from the very beginning?</color>
The dim yellow lights in the carriage reflect the shock and fear on every face, capturing those emotions and trapping them there like amber.
No one dares to move. No one dares to look away. They stare at the detective like prisoners awaiting judgment, eyes fixed on the judge's lips.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The Burning Redwood. It's a reference to a fire in the past—the one that happened to the Redwood Orphanage.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This was the only part of the letter that the victim tore out. She loved danger and craved thrills, but there was one thing she didn't want the detective to discover.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Which is the fact that the victim herself was the one responsible for the Redwood fire. She was the target of the killer's vengeance.
Then, who is the killer? Who is most likely to be seeking vengeance for Redwood on this train?

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We used the damaged watch, which has stopped at 1:05, to establish the time at which the crime took place. But... what if everything that happened afterward was a lie? What if it was all just staged to mislead us?
"Eliminate all impossibilities, and whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth."

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Now, let us make an even bolder hypothesis! The truth has been right in front of us all along—

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>We've all been deceived. The real crime occurred long before any of this chaos began.</color>
[Begin Small CG - Murder Process: Black Screen First]

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Let's go back to last night. Around 10 o'clock, the victim and the detective bid each other goodnight. Then they turned off the lights and went to sleep.
[Transition to Small CG 1: William Appears]

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Around 11:45, the power supply to the first-class carriage stopped once again for unknown reasons. The compartment was plunged into darkness.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Someone stepped out of their compartment and shut off the circuit breaker, creating the conditions for the crime. However, they accidentally smeared the paint on the breaker onto their hand.
[Murder Small CG 2: Train Attendant Allison Appears]

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: To ensure that the victim would remain completely unconscious, someone had slipped an overdose of sleeping pills into her nightcap beforehand.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She had been furious about the scheduling error. It was precisely this mistake that brought someone who was never supposed to be in the first-class carriage there. In other words, me.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But it didn't matter. The plan can still be salvaged. After all, they only needed to avoid the suite's parlor where I was. And so, the culprits gathered and made their way to Room 103, which was connected to the victim's room.
[Murder Small CG 3: Mrs. Jones Appears]

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: When they got there, the door to Room 103 had already been opened for them.

steps.speaker: Detective ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's very clever, really. After all, who would ever suspect a senile, frail old woman?
[Murder Small CG 4: The Group About to Turn the Doorknob]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The fire didn't kill everyone. There was far more than one survivor from Redwood. They had planned their vengeance, which is why they all gathered aboard the Praeva.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The midnight bell is about to ring... They, who thirst for vengeance, have gathered. After all these years, they can finally grab the knife—
[Murder Small CG 5: The Group About to Strike]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And kill the true culprit with their own hands.
[Red Flash + Black Screen, Repeated Knife Stabbing Sounds] [Hold Black Screen for Several Seconds, Then Slowly Fade Back to AVG]
[Back to Dining Car]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And with this, the truth finally comes to light.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This was an organized crime born in the name of vengeance. The victims of the Redwood Orphanage worked together and finally succeeded in killing the criminal who had escaped the punishment of law.
<i>The train continues onward through the night, but the expressions on the passengers' faces are no longer the same.
<i>Lowered heads lift, trembling hands turn still. No one refutes your words, and no one speaks to beg forgiveness. They simply stare at you in silence.
<i>Many things dwell in those gazes. Surprise, fear, anxiety, relief, exhaustion... and a trace of stubbornness and madness that could almost be called pride.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: As the only outsider in first class, you could have pinned all the suspicion on me, or weave countless lies to obstruct my investigation... but you didn't.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Instead, you hid all the clues between your words. Redwood, the orphanage, and every person who died in that fire... Even now, you're waiting for me to uncover the truth...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Just as... the one who wrote you.

<i>The lights turn hazy. The outlines of tables and cups begin to blur. The people who sat there mere moments ago fade from your sight one by one, like words on a page that are slowly being washed away by rain.
Until only one person remains at the far end of the dining car.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Most impressive. When did you figure it out?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: "Revenge" was a popular theme for a time before Nightfall. There's a community of detective novel enthusiasts on the dark web forums who've been railing against you for ages now.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Besides, you barely modified the story at all. It was far too easy to recognize.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I see... It seems I wasn't careful enough, then.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Congratulations, detective. You've uncovered every secret in the book and unraveled every truth. Now you can finally—

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Hm?

options: The truth I seek goes beyond this.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The story of Praeva might have concluded, but the same cannot be said about the one outside the book. Who exactly are you? Why did you write this book? These questions have troubled me for a while, and only now do I finally have the answer.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The <color=#fb9259>third answer</color>, hidden away within this story—
[Transition to CG - Modified Key Visual, Train Carriage Close-up]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That's right. Anyone could be the killer. Anyone could be lying.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The thrill of exposing lies can cloud one's judgment, causing them to overlook the fact that there's still one final deception in this story—
[Transition to CG - Modified Key Visual, Panoramic View]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The story of Redwood hasn't ended. It's still unfolding.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This is the final truth you've concealed. Your true purpose in writing the story of the Praeva—

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This book itself is your vengeance.
